```{r}
# Install packages to use

library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(TOSTER)
library(boot)

# Set working directory

my_wd <- "you/directory/here/arbor_lab/02"
```

```{r}
# We're using Forest Inventory and Analysis data from New York State.
# Read in tree data. These data only have live trees.
# Units are in kg C/tree.

tree <- read_csv(paste0(my_wd, "/data/fia_tree_carbon.csv")) 
```

```{r}
# View number of tree observations by species (top 10 within each forest type)

tree_spp <- tree |> 
  group_by(forest_type, COMMON_NAME) |> 
  summarize(num_trees = n()) |> 
  arrange(desc(num_trees)) |> 
  slice(1:10)
tree_spp

# Make a plot of number of trees by species within each forest type
ggplot(tree_spp, aes(x = reorder(COMMON_NAME, num_trees), y = num_trees)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  facet_wrap(~ forest_type, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "Number of trees") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14))
``` 

```{r}
# Calculate carbon at the stand level
# Multiply by tree expansion factor (x TPA_UNADJ), convert to metric tons (x 0.001), and apply CO2 conversion factor (x 3.664)

stand <- tree |> 
  group_by(forest_type, STATECD, COUNTYCD, PLOT, INVYR) |>
  summarize(jenkins = sum(carbon_total_jenkins*TPA_UNADJ)*0.001*3.664,
            crm = sum(carbon_total_crm*TPA_UNADJ)*0.001*3.664,
            nsvb = sum(carbon_total_nsvb*TPA_UNADJ)*0.001*3.664)    
stand
```

```{r}
# Visualize differences in carbon estimates at the stand level
# Format data "long" for plotting

stand_long <- stand |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(jenkins, crm, nsvb), names_to = "method", values_to = "carbon")

# Make a density plot of carbon estimates by method
ggplot(stand_long, aes(x = carbon, fill = method, color = method)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ forest_type) +
  labs(x = "Carbon (mtCO2e/ac)",
       y = "Density",
       fill = "Method",
       color = "Method") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14))
```


```{r}
# Method 1. Classic statistical test (t-test) 

# Get a dataset only for spruce-fir stands
stand_sf <- stand |> 
  filter(forest_type == "Spruce-fir")

# Check the normality of the differences
ggplot(stand_sf, aes(sample = jenkins - nsvb)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line(color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Theoretical quantiles",
       y = "Sample quantiles (Jenkins − NSVB, mtCO2e/ac)",
       title = "Normal Q-Q plot") +
  theme_bw()

# Conduct a paired t-test to compare the mean of the Jenkins and NSVB estimates for the spruce-fir forest type
t.test(stand_sf$jenkins, stand_sf$nsvb, paired = TRUE) 
```


```{r}
# Method 2. Equivalence tests (Two one-sided tests) 

# Examines whether the mean of the Jenkins estimates is equivalent to the mean of the NSVB estimates. 
# Define the equivalence margin as 20% of the standard deviation of the difference between both predictions
delta <- sd(stand_sf$jenkins - stand_sf$nsvb) * 0.2

# Set the TOST equivalence bounds and perform the test
tost_result <- tsum_TOST(
  m1 = mean(stand_sf$jenkins),      
  sd1 = sd(stand_sf$jenkins),
  n1 = nrow(stand_sf),

  m2 = mean(stand_sf$nsvb),  
  sd2 = sd(stand_sf$nsvb),  
  n2 = nrow(stand_sf),
  
  low_eqbound = -delta,
  high_eqbound = delta,
  eqbound_type = "raw"      
)

tost_result

# Conduct a paired t-test and visualize the 95% confidence interval for the mean difference
tt95 <- t.test(stand_sf$jenkins, stand_sf$nsvb, paired = TRUE) |>
  tidy()

# Plot the mean difference with the 95% confidence interval and equivalence region
ggplot(tt95, aes(y = "Jenkins − NSVB")) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -delta, xmax = delta, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "blue", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(x = estimate, xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
                  linewidth = 0.8, size = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-delta * 1.5, max(tt95$conf.high, delta) * 1.2)) +
  labs(x = "Mean difference (mtCO2e/ac)", y = NULL,
       title = "Equivalence test (TOST)",
       caption = "Shaded = equivalence region (+/- delta)") +
  theme_bw()
```


```{r}
# Method 3. Bootstrap resampling

# Bootstrap confidence interval for the mean 
boot_mean <- function(data, indices) {
  mean(data[indices])
}

# Calculate bootstrap confidence intervals for each estimate

set.seed(11252026)
run_boot_ci <- function(data, label, R = 5000) {
  b <- boot(data = data, statistic = boot_mean, R = R)
  ci <- boot.ci(b, type = "perc") 
  tibble(
    dataset = label,
    boot_mean = mean(b$t),
    lower_95 = ci$percent[4],
    upper_95 = ci$percent[5]
  )
}

# Run for each dataset
boot_jenkins <- run_boot_ci(stand_sf$jenkins, "Jenkins")
boot_nsvb <- run_boot_ci(stand_sf$nsvb, "NSVB")
boot_combined <- run_boot_ci(stand_sf$jenkins - stand_sf$nsvb, "Difference")

boot_summary <- rbind(boot_jenkins, boot_nsvb, boot_combined)
boot_summary

# Reorder datasets for plotting
boot_summary <- boot_summary %>%
  mutate(dataset = factor(dataset, levels = c("Difference", "Jenkins", "NSVB")))

# Plot differences in bootstrapped means
ggplot(boot_summary, aes(x = dataset, y = boot_mean, color = dataset)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_95, ymax = upper_95), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", boot_mean)),
    vjust = -1.2, size = 3.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals",
       caption = "Bootstrap mean with 95% confidence intervals",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Mean CO2 (mtCO2-e/ac)") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
